issues.body:
Adding `dp-planner` to the server default set changes execution (DPccp bushy tree for connected BGPs of 3..=63 patterns, crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:6944 and :7682) but NOT the explain surfaces.

- crates/sparq-engine/src/explain.rs:320 unconditionally emits `BGP [binary join plan: greedy GOO ordering] (N patterns)` and then replays the GOO loop (`exec::goo_seed`, `exec::goo_seed_sort`, ...) to print the join order.
- crates/sparq-engine/src/explain_json.rs labels the node `BGP [binary GOO]` and builds the tree from the algebra plus `exec::bgp_estimate`, not from `dp::plan`.
- Neither file contains any reference to `dp::`/`DPccp`.

Consequences on the shipped binary (both surfaces are default-on: text explain always, `explain-json` in the default set):
1. `GET /sparql?explain=true` and `Accept: text/x-sparq-explain` describe a greedy left-deep plan while a bushy DP plan executes.
2. `explain=analyze` / the `explain-json` analyze mode attach `actual`, `nanos` and `qError` to a GOO-shaped tree, so the GUI plan-explorer heat map attributes measured time and q-error to operators that did not run.

This directly contradicts the PR's own framing ("Default-on measured-plan parity", "HTTP uses the same plans as the CLI/canonical benchmarks") — plan *execution* moves toward parity while plan *reporting* becomes wrong.

CI does not catch it: crates/sparq-server/tests/explain_metrics.rs:38 JOIN_QUERY is a 2-pattern BGP, and `dp::plan` declines below 3 patterns (crates/sparq-engine/src/dp.rs:507), so `assert!(body.contains("BGP [binary join plan: greedy GOO ordering]"))` at explain_metrics.rs:77 still passes. The divergence is invisible to the default lane.

Note this is pre-existing for sparq-cli (which already hard-enables `dp-planner`); this PR extends it to the network-facing server, where EXPLAIN is a documented user-facing endpoint.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) make the explain surfaces DP-aware — call `dp::active()` + `dp::plan` in explain.rs/explain_json.rs and render the returned `JoinTree`, labelling it e.g. `BGP [binary join plan: DPccp bushy ordering]` with the greedy label retained for the decline path; or (b) if that is out of scope for this bead, at minimum add a `#[cfg(feature = "dp-planner")]` caveat line in the explain output ("NOTE: DPccp is active; the order shown is the greedy replay") and file a bead for the real fix. Whichever path is taken, add a server test with a >=3-pattern connected BGP that pins the explain text under the default feature set, so the divergence cannot ship silently again.
issues.title: Default-on dp-planner makes the server's EXPLAIN / explain-json report a plan that is not executed

issues.body:
The new README bullet claims: "so HTTP uses the same plans as the CLI/canonical benchmarks." skills/http-server/SKILL.md repeats it as "matching the CLI and canonical benchmark binary."

crates/sparq-cli/Cargo.toml:146 pins the engine as `features = ["dp-planner", "algebra-rewrite", "antijoin-static-decline"]`. The server default set after this PR is `["server", "jsonld", "dp-planner", "algebra-rewrite", "explain-json"]` — no `antijoin-static-decline`.

Per its own feature comment (crates/sparq-engine/Cargo.toml:192-208), `antijoin-static-decline` is "a pure evaluation-ORDERING change" that makes `try_theta_antijoin` decline before evaluating the left side, eliminating a duplicate BGP evaluation on the `Filter(!bound, LeftJoin(...))` shape. Result-equivalent, but a different executed plan.

The canonical query benchmarks build sparq-cli with default features (e.g. scripts/bench/materialize-same-box.sh:126, scripts/bench/bytes-per-triple.sh:54) and the canonical HTTP bench builds sparq-server with default features (scripts/bench/canonical-http-gather-instance.sh:39). So the two binaries still diverge on this axis, and an unqualified "same plans" claim is an overclaim in a repo whose honesty rules forbid exactly this.
issues.fix_hint: Either add `antijoin-static-decline` to the server's default set (with its own forwarding feature + comment, matching the pattern used for `dp-planner`), or downgrade the wording in both crates/sparq-server/README.md and skills/http-server/SKILL.md to something precise, e.g. "HTTP now matches the CLI on join ordering and the algebra-rewrite pass; `antijoin-static-decline` remains CLI-only (bead <id>)."
issues.title: "HTTP uses the same plans as the CLI/canonical benchmarks" is still not true — antijoin-static-decline is missing

issues.body:
The module doc says "Tripwire that the server's default feature set forwards the engine's DPccp join-order planner." But the file is gated `#![cfg(feature = "dp-planner")]`, so the regression it names — someone drops `dp-planner` from `default` in crates/sparq-server/Cargo.toml:53 — compiles the entire file away and `cargo test -p sparq-server` goes green with zero tests registered. The tripwire fires only on a broken *forwarding edge* (`dp-planner = ["sparq-engine/dp-planner"]`), not on a broken *default set*.

The sibling crates/sparq-server/tests/algebra_rewrite_default.rs has the same structural limitation but documents it explicitly across ~10 lines of module doc ("dropping `algebra-rewrite` from `default` makes the default lanes silently skip it...") plus a note on whole-workspace feature unification. The new file's two-line justification ("gated on the server's forwarding feature so deliberate lean builds remain valid") does not disclose the hole, so the headline claim reads stronger than what is enforced.
issues.fix_hint: Mirror the sibling's honest module doc: state that the gate means a `default`-set removal silently skips this test, that the enforced property is the forwarding edge only, and that the per-crate `cargo test -p sparq-server` lanes (which never pass `--no-default-features`) are where it is authoritative. Alternatively drop the word "default feature set" from the headline and call it a forwarding tripwire.
issues.title: The "default feature set" tripwire does not detect removal from the default set

issues.body:
`dp_planner_is_forwarded_and_default_query_is_result_equivalent` compares `result_bag(...)` against `sparq_engine::without_dp_planner(|| result_bag(...))` on a 3-triple fixture and a 3-pattern linear chain that yields exactly one row.

Nothing in the test observes whether the DP path was actually taken. If `dp::plan` declined for any reason (budget, pattern count, disconnected graph — crates/sparq-engine/src/dp.rs:505-534), both sides would run identical greedy GOO code and the assertion would still pass. A mutation that disabled DP entirely inside the engine would leave this test green. The `!planned.is_empty()` assertion only guards against an empty fixture.

So the only load-bearing content is the compile-time symbol witness on `without_dp_planner`; the behavioural half is decorative. The genuine differential coverage already lives in crates/sparq-engine/tests/dp_planner_differential.rs, tests/dp_default.rs and tests/proptest_eval.rs:846, which is fine — but the test's doc comment ("plus a real query-path equivalence check") claims more than the assertions deliver.
issues.fix_hint: Either make the behavioural half observable — e.g. assert via the explain surface that the executed plan differs between the two scopes, or use a shape/fixture where DPccp and greedy GOO demonstrably produce different orders and non-trivial multi-row bags (exercising bag multiplicity, not a single row) — or reword the doc comment to describe it accurately as a compile-time forwarding witness with a smoke-level sanity query.
issues.title: The result-equivalence half cannot distinguish DPccp firing from DPccp declining

issues.body:
This flips DPccp on by default for the one crate that accepts queries from untrusted callers. Per-request planning cost is now bounded by the compiled-in defaults rather than by anything the operator can tune: `DEFAULT_MAX_SUBGRAPHS = 4096` and `PAIR_BUDGET_FACTOR = 128` (crates/sparq-engine/src/dp.rs:65, :80), i.e. up to 4096 DP-table entries and 524288 emitted csg/cmp pairs materialised into a `Vec` and sorted (dp.rs:529-534), for every BGP of 3..=63 patterns in every request.

The budgets do bound it — this is not unbounded blow-up — but it is a real per-request CPU/allocation multiplier versus greedy on a path an attacker controls, and it is cheap to trigger with a moderately dense hand-written BGP. The new feature comment (Cargo.toml:77-80), the README bullet and the SKILL blockquote all frame the change purely as measurement parity and say nothing about planner cost, nor about whether the server's query timeout / `QueryBudget` cancel flag covers the planning phase at all (the DP enumeration in dp.rs shows no deadline or cancellation check).

The CLI and sparq-py, which already enable this, are local/trusted callers — the server is not, so the risk profile is genuinely new here.
issues.fix_hint: Confirm whether the server's query timeout covers planning; if it does not, either wrap the server's query path in `with_dp_planner_budget(<smaller server-side budget>, ...)` or add a cancellation/deadline check to the DPccp enumeration loop. At minimum, document the planner-cost consideration in the `dp-planner` feature comment and the SKILL security posture section, and note the escape hatch (`--no-default-features --features server,jsonld`) as a hardening option rather than only as a benchmarking one.
issues.title: Planner-cost amplification on an untrusted network input path is not considered or documented

verdict.summary:
The mechanics are sound: sparq-engine exposes `dp-planner = []` (engine Cargo.toml:172), the forwarding edge is correct, DPccp is order-only (a BGP is a commutative/associative natural join) and is differentially tested in the engine, and the thread-local install state defaults to Enabled on every thread so tokio/rayon workers pick it up. sparq-core/sparq-engine are direct deps so the new test resolves. No new dependency; no golden feature-matrix leg needed (default-on features are not listed there).

Two problems block approval.

(1) EXPLAIN now reports a plan that is not the plan that runs. explain.rs:320 hard-codes "BGP [binary join plan: greedy GOO ordering]" then replays the GOO loop to print the order; explain_json.rs labels "BGP [binary GOO]" and builds its tree from the algebra + `bgp_estimate`. Neither file references `dp::` at all. Before this PR the server did not compile `dp-planner`, so its explain output was accurate; now `?explain=true`, `Accept: text/x-sparq-explain` and the default-on `explain-json` tree all describe a greedy left-deep plan while 3+-pattern BGPs execute a DPccp bushy tree, and `explain=analyze` attaches `actual`/`nanos`/`qError` to operators that did not run. The PR headline is "Default-on measured-plan parity"; this breaks explain parity on a default surface. CI misses it: explain_metrics.rs JOIN_QUERY is a 2-pattern BGP, below `dp::plan`'s >=3 gate, so it ships silently.

(2) The parity claim is an overclaim. sparq-cli/Cargo.toml:146 hard-enables `dp-planner`, `algebra-rewrite` AND `antijoin-static-decline`; the server default set has only the first two. `antijoin-static-decline` is an evaluation-ordering change, so "HTTP uses the same plans as the CLI/canonical benchmarks" remains false in a checkable way.

Three minor issues on the new test and on planner cost follow.
